subject: GST passthrough mechanics for multi-entity reseller credit flow
messages:
From: accounts@novumenergy.com (Novum Energy Finance)
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: rajiv.singh@novumenergy.com
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Query: How should we reflect APAC GST on reseller credit for Aug invoice?

Hi Priyom,

We're finalising payment for Redwood's August invoice but hit a snag on the reseller credit line where Mallory Marketplace passed through a referral fee. Our local APAC accounting team is asking whether this should be treated as a GST-inclusive expense on our side, or if the reverse-charge applies because Mallory is an overseas marketplace entity.

Invoice attached (CSV export) shows: line 3 — "Marketplace referral credit" net USD 9,000. No VAT number provided by Mallory in the invoice extract. Can Redwood confirm:
- Should Novum apply reverse-charge (self-account) in India/NZ for this credit?
- Do you require Mallory's VAT/GST registration for us to withhold tax?
- Any special invoice wording we should expect from Redwood when the reverse-charge is applied?

Appreciate a quick steer — we're on a 10-Sep payment run.

Thanks,
Asha Rao
Senior GL Manager, Novum Energy
accounts@novumenergy.com

Attachment: novum-invoice-20250831.csv

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: accounts@novumenergy.com (accounts@novumenergy.com)
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Query: How should we reflect APAC GST on reseller credit for Aug invoice?

Hi Asha — thanks for the note and for attaching the CSV. Looping in Ben (billing ops) and Vanessa (finance) who handle multi-entity splits and APAC GST flows.

Quick answers up front:
- In many APAC jurisdictions, reverse-charge/self-accounting can apply when a local entity receives services from an overseas marketplace that does not have local GST registration.
- We need to confirm whether Mallory supplied a GST/VAT registration that covers the Novum jurisdiction. If Mallory does not have a local GST number, the buyer (Novum) often records the tax via reverse-charge.
- Redwood can emit an invoice variant that includes the phrasing "Reverse charge – recipient to account for GST" and a breakdown of taxable base per local law, but we need to confirm the contractual path (did Mallory bill Novum directly and Redwood only credits a referral?)

Ben/Vanessa — can you advise if Mallory was billed directly by Novum or if the referral credit was a passthrough on the Redwood invoice? Also attaching our RC template for Novum to review.

Best,
Priyom Das
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Attachment: rc-instruction-template.pdf

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, accounts@novumenergy.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Query: How should we reflect APAC GST on reseller credit for Aug invoice?

Thanks Priyom. I pulled the transaction log. Short version: Mallory was the party that collected the fee from Novum via its marketplace flow; Redwood recorded a contra-revenue (referral credit) to Novum as a line item because Mallory remitted referral proceeds to us earlier in the month and we netted the credit. So Novum received a credit from Redwood, not a direct invoice from Mallory.

Implications:
- If Mallory did not present a GST registration number for the jurisdiction, then Novum likely needs to apply reverse-charge/self-accounting on their side for tax reporting.
- Redwood can issue a reissued invoice that explicitly calls out: "Credit issued for marketplace referral — reverse-charge may apply; consult local tax guidance" and include the amount, original invoice ref, and the net amount per jurisdiction.

I recommend this path for minimal friction: Redwood issues a re-issued credit note that mirrors the CSV line and includes the reverse-charge note. That should be sufficient for most APAC GL teams to post the credit and self-account.

I'm attaching the ledger extract (redacted PII) and a suggested invoice wording.

Ben Carter
Billing Ops, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: billing-ledger-extract-aug2025.csv

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: accounts@novumenergy.com (accounts@novumenergy.com), priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Sep 2025 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Query: How should we reflect APAC GST on reseller credit for Aug invoice?

Hi Asha / team — Vanessa here from Finance. 

Operational note and workaround: if Novum needs a clear audit trail for the payment run on 10-Sep, we can do a two-step approach so your AP team doesn't have to delay payment:
1) We will reissue a credit memo (PDF) dated 31-Aug showing the referral credit line and include the line "Reverse charge – recipient to self-assess GST where applicable."
2) Separately, we will send a short group of supporting docs: (a) ledger extract demonstrating Mallory's referral remittance to Redwood, (b) email trail from Mallory confirming they did not provide a local GST registration when they collected the fee.

Please confirm if that satisfies your AR controls. If Novum needs us to withhold any portion or produce a tax withholding certificate, note that Redwood cannot act as the withholding agent for Mallory — the buyer's reverse-charge/self-assessment is the typical path.

If helpful, we can also run a split invoice per country for the marketplace credit (i.e., separate line for NZ, AU, IN taxable base) — but that will take 2 business days.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Accounting Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-rc-support.zip (contains: ledger-extract.pdf, mallory-email-redacted.txt)
